patterns.name: Breakout + Retest Pattern
patterns.overview: The Breakout + Retest pattern occurs when price breaks above a key resistance level and then pulls back (retests) that level. If the retest holds as support, price is likely to continue in the direction of the breakout.
characteristics: Occurs in an uptrend
Breakout above a key resistance
Price pulls back to retest the broken resistance
Retest holds as new support
Continuation of the uptrend
Volume decreases on retest and increases on continuation
key_points: Breakout above key resistance is important
Retest confirms the level as new support
Lower volume on retest adds reliability
Higher volume on continuation confirms strength

patterns.name: Breakdown + Retest Pattern (Bearish)
patterns.overview: The Breakdown + Retest pattern occurs when price breaks below a key support level and then pulls back to retest that level (now acting as resistance). If the retest fails, price is likely to continue moving down.
characteristics: Occurs in a downtrend or after range breakdown
Price breaks below a key support level
Pulls back to retest the broken support (now resistance)
Retest gets rejected
Price continues downward
Volume increases on breakdown and on continuation
key_points: Break below key support is the first confirmation
Retest of broken support as resistance is the key setup
Rejection at retest confirms seller control
Volume should be higher on breakdown and continuation

patterns.name: Head and Shoulders (Bearish)
patterns.overview: The Head and Shoulders is a bearish reversal pattern that forms after an uptrend. It consists of three peaks: a higher peak (Head) between two lower peaks (Shoulders). A breakdown below the neckline confirms the pattern and signals a potential downtrend.
characteristics: Occurs after an uptrend
Three peaks: Left Shoulder, higher Head, Right Shoulder
Neckline connects the lows between the peaks
Breakdown below neckline confirms the pattern
Volume increases on breakdown
Price target is the height of the head projected downward
key_points: Forms after an uptrend
Head is the highest peak
Shoulders are lower than head
Neckline connects the lows
Breakdown below neckline is key
Volume increases on breakdown

patterns.name: Double Top Pattern
patterns.overview: The Double Top is a bearish reversal pattern that forms after an uptrend. It consists of two attempts to break a resistance level followed by a breakdown below the neckline support, signaling a potential trend reversal to the downside.
characteristics: Occurs after an uptrend
Two distinct highs at the same resistance level
Neckline connects the lows between the two highs
Breakdown below neckline confirms the pattern
Volume decreases on the second top
Volume increases on breakdown
key_points: Forms after a clear uptrend
Two tops at the same resistance level
Neckline connects the lows
Breakdown below neckline confirms bearish reversal
Higher volume on breakdown adds reliability

patterns.name: Double Bottom Pattern
patterns.overview: The Double Bottom is a bullish reversal pattern that forms after a downtrend. It consists of two tests of a support level followed by a breakout above the neckline (resistance). The breakout signals a potential trend reversal and the start of a new uptrend.
characteristics: Occurs after a downtrend
Two distinct lows at the same support level
Neckline connects the highs between the two bottoms
Breakout occurs above neckline
Volume decreases during formation and increases on breakout
key_points: Forms after a clear downtrend
Two bottoms should be at the same support level
Breakout above neckline confirms the pattern
Higher volume on breakout increases reliability

patterns.name: Cup and Handle Pattern
patterns.overview: The Cup and Handle is a bullish continuation pattern that forms in an uptrend. It consists of a rounded bottom (cup) followed by a small consolidation (handle). A breakout above the handle high signals the continuation of the uptrend.
characteristics: Occurs in an uptrend
Cup forms a U-shaped rounded bottom
Handle forms a small downward consolidation
Breakout occurs above handle high
Volume decreases in handle and increases on breakout
key_points: Higher success rate when pattern forms after a strong uptrend
Ideal handle forms in the upper half of the cup
Breakout with high volume increases reliability

patterns.name: Bull Flag Pattern
patterns.overview: A Bull Flag is a continuation pattern that forms after a strong upward move (flagpole) followed by a small downward consolidation (flag). The breakout from the flag signals the continuation of the uptrend.
characteristics: Occurs in an uptrend
Sharp upward move (flagpole)
Small downward consolidation (flag)
Breakout above resistance (flag high)
Volume decreases during flag formation and increases on breakout
key_points: Strong uptrend before the flag is essential
Flag slopes slightly downward or sideways
Breakout with high volume increases reliability

patterns.name: Bear Flag Pattern
patterns.overview: The Bear Flag is a bearish continuation pattern that forms after a strong downward move (flagpole) followed by a small upward consolidation (flag). The breakdown below the flag signals the continuation of the downtrend.
characteristics: Occurs in a downtrend
Sharp downward move (flagpole)
Small upward consolidation (flag) with parallel channel
Breakdown below flag support
Volume decreases during flag formation and increases on breakdown
key_points: Strong downtrend before the flag is essential
Flag slopes slightly upward or moves sideways
Breakdown below flag support confirms continuation
Higher volume on breakdown increases reliability

patterns.name: Bull Pennant Pattern
patterns.overview: The Bull Pennant is a continuation pattern that forms after a strong uptrend (flagpole) followed by a small symmetrical consolidation (pennant). A breakout above the pennant resistance signals the continuation of the uptrend.
characteristics: Occurs in an uptrend
Sharp upward move (flagpole)
Small consolidation in a symmetrical triangle (pennant)
Lower highs and higher lows during consolidation
Breakout above pennant resistance
Volume decreases during pennant and increases on breakout
key_points: Strong uptrend before the pennant is essential
Pennant forms with lower highs and higher lows
Volume decreases during pennant formation
Breakout with high volume increases reliability

patterns.name: Bear Pennant Pattern
patterns.overview: The Bear Pennant is a continuation pattern that occurs after a strong downtrend (flagpole) followed by a small symmetrical consolidation (pennant). A breakdown below the pennant support signals the continuation of the downtrend.
characteristics: Occurs in a downtrend
Sharp downward move (flagpole)
Small consolidation in a symmetrical triangle (pennant)
Lower highs and lower lows during consolidation
Breakdown below pennant support
Volume decreases during pennant and increases on breakdown
key_points: Strong downtrend before the pennant is essential
Pennant forms with lower highs and lower lows
Volume decreases during pennant formation
Breakdown with high volume increases reliability
Price likely continues in the direction of the breakdown
